coupling: GetDataSlab's rank-N copier (GET_DATA_SLABN) reads a strided selection from a buffer allocated to the product of the dimensions. Three edits each advance the dim-0 source index by one element, and each edit is in range on its own because it reserves or consumes only a single trailing element. 6d38a5c adds (stride[0] > 1) to every sample and, for rank != 2 and stride > 1, replaces the inclusive dim-0 check (edge-1) <= (dims-1-start)/stride with edge <= (dims-start)/stride. That product check leaves stride-1 elements past the unshifted last index, which for the usual stride of 2 is exactly the one element the new term reads; stride 1 still adds nothing and still uses the old check. 51da9bb then increments only the last sample, and only when that unshifted last index is at most dims-2. fac7634 applies the same headroom test to the running origin before the sample loop. Neither later test looks at the other adjustments, only at the caller's start, stride, and edge. A length-5 vector read as start 1, stride 2, edge 2 (one-based x(2:2:4); rank 3 with trailing singletons so the copy stays on the rank-N path, from a zlib-compressed cell preloaded by Mat_VarReadInfo) is accepted by both the inclusive check and the tightened product check, and both headroom tests see unshifted last index 3 <= 5-2. Each edit therefore contributes +1. One of them reads index 4, inside the 5-double allocation. Any two read index 5, eight bytes past it. Dropping any one edit leaves the other two, so the overflow is still reachable; the total phase has to be reconciled with the single element of headroom, which is not local to one diff.
